truth_claims.note: conf=0.93; The EPUB's title/author metadata are swapped and garbled ("Charles Stross - Lobsters 04" / "Halo"). The work is "Halo," a novelette by Charles Stross, first published in Asimov's Science Fiction, June 2002, and a Hugo/Sturgeon nominee. ISFDB records it as Series: Macx Family, Series Number: 4 — the nine-story sequence (Lobsters, Troubadour, Tourist, Halo, Router, Nightfall, Curator, Elector, Survivor) later fixed up into the 2005 novel Accelerando. The filename's "Lobsters 04" is an informal fan-naming of the same sequence after its first installment; equivalent series names in use are "Accelerando" / "Macx Family." Not a standalone novel; the 2011 date is the ebook packaging date, not first publication.

"Lobsters 04" is not a published series; it is a fan-made label derived from the first story of the sequence. The canonical series per ISFDB is "Macx Family," in which Halo is #4 (Lobsters, Troubadour, Tourist, Halo, Router, Nightfall, Curator, Elector, Survivor). The nine stories were later combined into the fix-up novel Accelerando (2005); Macx Family is the tighter/verified series designation. Halo first appeared in Asimov's SF, June 2002 (Hugo and Sturgeon nominee); the 2011 date in the filename reflects an ebook repackaging, not first publication. No ISBN for the standalone novelette.
